chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Aban al-Ahmar, from Ziyad ibn Abi Raja', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
What you know, say it; and what you do not know, say: God knows best.
Indeed, a man snatches a verse from the Quran and falls because of it farther than the distance between the sky and the earth.

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ: 'Allah knows best' — the proper response when one lacks knowledge
key_terms.يَنْتَزِعُ الْآيَةَ: To snatch/pull out a verse — taking a Quranic verse out of its context to misuse it

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about speaking without knowledge of the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) warns against speaking about the Quran without knowledge. The teaching prohibits issuing opinions on Quranic verses beyond one's understanding and advises one to simply say 'God knows best' when uncertain. The vivid imagery of falling a distance greater than between heaven and earth illustrates the gravity of misinterpreting divine scripture.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khallad, from Al Hassan Bin Al Al Washha, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Ziyad Bin Abu Raja’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
As for what you know, so you can talk about it, but what you do not know, so you should be saying, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Knowing’.
The man clinches to a Verse from the Quran, and falls in it (to a distance) further than what is between the sky and the earth’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people has narrated has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washshi’ from Aban al-Ahmar from Ziyad ibn abu Raja’ from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“What you know you may speak it up but what you do not know say, ‘Allah knows best’.
A man refers to a verse in the holy Quran and gives it a meaning that is farther from the truth than the heavens are from earth.”
